_notes: Plot-level secrets written for this study (2026-10-05). 12 premises, 4 candidate final-scene twists each. Twists within a premise are meant to be about equally compatible with the premise.

items.premise: A new keeper arrives at a remote lighthouse to replace a man who vanished a month earlier.
twists: The previous keeper never left: he has been hiding in the lighthouse cellar all along.
The new keeper is the vanished man's estranged child, who came to find out what happened.
The lighthouse was decommissioned years ago and no ships pass any more; the job is a fiction kept up by the villagers.
The new keeper caused the previous keeper's death and took the post to destroy the evidence.

items.premise: Four old university friends meet for a reunion dinner at a restaurant ten years after graduating.
twists: One of the four died a year ago, and the others are imagining her presence at the table.
The host has gathered them to confess that he stole the idea that made him rich from one of the others.
The dinner is being secretly filmed for a television programme, and one friend is in on it.
Two of the friends have been secretly married to each other for years.

items.premise: A woman inherits her late grandmother's house in the countryside and goes to clear it out.
twists: The grandmother is not dead: she staged her death to escape a debt and is watching from the neighbouring farm.
The woman discovers she was adopted and the 'grandmother' was in fact her birth mother.
The house is worthless, but the grandmother spent decades as a celebrated forger and the attic is full of fake paintings.
The friendly neighbour who helps her has been stealing from the house every night.

items.premise: A small scientific team spends the winter at an isolated Antarctic research station.
twists: The team's supply flights stopped because, unknown to them, the funding institute has shut down and no one is coming.
One team member has been falsifying the data the whole season.
The 'researchers' are subjects of a psychology experiment on isolation, and the station is in a warehouse in Norway.
The station doctor is not a doctor at all, but an impostor who took a dead man's identity.

items.premise: A detective is called to a quiet seaside town to investigate the theft of a famous painting from the local museum.
twists: The detective stole the painting herself and is steering the investigation away from the truth.
The painting was never stolen: the museum director hid it to claim the insurance money.
The stolen painting was a copy; the original was sold decades ago by the town's founding family.
The thief is the detective's own long-lost brother, who wanted to be found.

items.premise: On the morning of her wedding, a bride gets ready at a country hotel with her family around her.
twists: The groom has already fled the country the night before, and only the bride's sister knows.
The bride is planning to leave before the ceremony and has a train ticket hidden in her bag.
The wedding is a staged ceremony for the bride's dying father; the couple actually broke up months ago.
The bride and groom are both undercover police officers, and the wedding is a trap for one of the guests.

items.premise: A beloved teacher is spending his last week at a village school before retiring.
twists: The teacher never had any teaching qualification and has lived forty years under a borrowed name.
The school is closing for good and the teacher has known for months but told no one.
The teacher is not retiring by choice: he is going to prison for a crime he committed to protect a pupil.
The teacher has secretly paid for the education of half the village's children with lottery winnings.

items.premise: A cargo ship's crew picks up a lone survivor drifting in a lifeboat in the middle of the ocean.
twists: The survivor deliberately sank his own ship and killed its crew.
The survivor is a marine insurance investigator who staged the rescue to get aboard and inspect the cargo.
The survivor is the captain's son, whom the captain abandoned as a baby.
The lifeboat belongs to a ship that sank fifty years ago, and the survivor has not aged.

items.premise: A young man takes over his family's failing bakery after his father falls ill.
twists: The father is not ill: he invented the illness to force his son to come home.
The bakery has been a front for the family's illegal betting business for three generations.
The rival bakery across the street, which is driving them out of business, is secretly owned by his own mother.
The famous family recipe was stolen from the rival bakery fifty years ago.

items.premise: An elderly widow starts receiving unsigned letters that describe moments from her past in exact detail.
twists: She is writing the letters herself during episodes she does not remember.
The letters are from her husband, who wrote them before he died and arranged for them to be posted.
The letters come from a daughter she gave up for adoption sixty years ago.
The letters are written by her postman, who has been reading her old diaries, which he stole.

items.premise: An unknown teenager enters a prestigious chess tournament and starts beating grandmasters.
twists: The teenager is being fed moves by a hidden accomplice using a computer.
The teenager is the unacknowledged child of the reigning champion.
The teenager is losing her eyesight and plays the whole tournament from memory.
The grandmasters have been paid by a sponsor to lose to her.

items.premise: A journalist travels to a mountain village to write about its famous annual festival.
twists: The festival was invented ten years ago by the village council to attract tourists, and its 'ancient history' is fake.
The journalist was born in this village and was taken away as a small child after a scandal.
The journalist has come to expose the mayor for embezzlement, and the festival article is a cover.
The festival commemorates a landslide that the villagers caused themselves and blamed on an innocent man.
